verdict: revise (below threshold 7.5): a carefully scoped, unusually transparent simulation study with one confirmed core decision; the remaining gap is mainly missing analyses that the existing replays already support, plus readability, while the larger external-validity gaps need new evidence
strengths: Clear, well-motivated problem: a distribution-free slip bound for minimal-force grasping, compared against the strongest non-tactile conformal baseline, which was selected on a disjoint selection split before calibration or test data were read. This is a stronger and fairer comparator than an uncalibrated controller.

Statistically careful certificate. CRC is applied to the monotonised physical slip loss rather than to bisection labels, the CRC precondition and fallback are stated explicitly, the paper reports that the fallback never fired, and 'certified' is consistently defined as a marginal, in-expectation, per-stratum bound rather than a per-deployment guarantee.

Exemplary honesty about the confirmatory record. One of four core decisions is confirmed (H2a), H1 and H2b are not, and H3 is inconclusive. All eight deviations from the pre-registration are listed, including the post hoc CRC route, the 08c grid-floor defect that biases H2b, the dropped Holm correction, and the pilot-driven amendment that introduced the probe arm.

The headline result is large and robust across many views. D = 0.4168 [0.3484, 0.4778] holds under F*_lo/F*_hi, the label route, the post hoc grid, seeds 1-4, the Mondrian comparator and n = 50 calibration, and the tail ratio T = 0.59. The probe arm also slips less than the baseline, so the comparison is not bought with extra risk.

The ablation chain is interpreted with appropriate scoping. The paper explicitly says that 'static touch adds nothing' is a simulator consistency check (normal reading = F0, shear = m g/2), not a finding about real tactile sensors. It also reports a regime where the method loses (H2-R, D = -0.2614).

The intrinsic detector error is characterised in detail (correlation 0.948, bias +0.319, SD 0.110, a per-family SD showing capsules at 0.196, and a correlation of the error with log mu) and linked to the residual D-mu, the weak D3 cells and the H2-R reversal. The paper also states the limits of D-mu as a diagnostic.

Numbers are internally consistent across the abstract, the text, the tables and the figure prompt. Split sizes check out (n = 500 per stratum, 2,800 test instances, 2,096 and 1,500 stream instances), as does F0 = 9.81/0.3 = 32.7 N. Reproducibility detail (hyperparameters, seeds, compute, simulator settings) is good.
weaknesses: [evidence-level] The paper is simulation-only, with a rigid-contact MuJoCo model, rigid primitive objects and a modelled detector. The primary noise level sigma = 0.2 is assumed, not measured, and the effect falls to D = 0.14 (lower limit below the SESOI) at sigma = 0.4. Whether the headline survives on a real sensor is therefore unknown, and it is the most decision-relevant open question.

[evidence-level] Part of the margin comes from the design of the instance distribution: friction is drawn independently of every non-tactile input. The comparator set contains no non-tactile baseline with a noisy friction proxy (for example vision or category priors), no 'probe plus hand-set margin' practitioner rule, and no reactive slip-tightening controller. The 42 % figure is therefore an upper-end estimate tied to this distribution.

[evidence-level] The online study (H3) is underpowered (CI half-widths 0.15-0.20 against a projected 0.12) and confounded by unequal oracle/tracker slip rates in S1 and S2. Its feedback is the simulator's label rule, with physical audits on only one ordering. Frozen calibration does not fail under S2, so the rescue is shown for two of three shifts, and in S2 the tracker's force cost lies above the oracle's.
[evidence-level] The trackers are warm-started from the label-route q-hat rather than the CRC lambda-hat, so the online section does not test the primary certificate's behaviour under shift.

[paper-level] Two analyses that the existing grid replays already allow are missing. The pre-registered risk-efficiency frontier would compare the arms at matched realised slip; the argument that 'unequal slip makes D conservative' is plausible but informal, and the frontier would settle it. A high-probability (training-conditional, e.g. LTT/UCB) certificate is also not computed, although per-stratum baseline slip exceeds alpha in two strata.

[paper-level] The method's identity is diffuse. The headline arm is CertGrip-full (learned), yet onset-only (RE 0.4336) and the plug-in CSF-mu-hat perform as well or better, and the paper concludes that the operative method is 'probe + either rule + CRC'. The direct comparison CSF-mu-hat vs CSF-1, which is arguably the simplest statement of the contribution, is not given as a headline row with its own CI.

[paper-level] Readability is hampered by internal pipeline labels (07, 08a, 08c, 08e, 08f-08h), many hypothesis codes (H2-C, H2-H, H2-R, H2-T, H2-M, H2-n, H3-B, H3-L, H3-S, H4a-e, UT3) and hedged multi-clause sentences. An external reader must track a large private vocabulary, and the main message gets buried under caveats.

[paper-level] Table 2 labels the label-route H2b row 'equivalence (secondary)', while the text says H2b is not confirmed and that equivalence is not claimed. This is consistent once read carefully, but it invites misreading.

[paper-level] Literature coverage is self-admittedly incomplete. Classic work on friction estimation from incipient slip and on human grip-force regulation (e.g. Johansson/Westling-style grip-load coupling, early incipient-slip sensing) is not discussed, and many cited works are very recent, which leaves the novelty of 'lower the force until slip to read friction' under-contextualised.

[paper-level] Figure 1 exists only as a generation prompt inside the manuscript, and panel (b) is explicitly schematic. A rendered figure built from the actual per-stratum risk curves would add real evidence at no new cost.

[paper-level] The mechanisms behind the weak D3 cells, the D2 concentration of monotonicity violations and the H2-R reversal are all left untested. Some could be probed on the existing data, for example by stratifying the H2-R loss by detector error or by family, or by comparing the D3 margin with hidden-amplitude variance.
required_actions: [paper-level] Compute and show the pre-registered risk-efficiency frontier (RE against realised physical slip over the lambda grid / alpha grid) for CertGrip-full, CSF-mu-hat, onset-only and CSF-1 from the existing replays. Use it to replace the informal 'D is conservative' argument with a matched-risk comparison.

[paper-level] Compute a high-probability per-stratum certificate (e.g. Learn-then-Test or a binomial upper confidence bound on the monotonised risk) from the existing grid replays, and report the resulting force cost next to the in-expectation CRC result.

[paper-level] Add an explicit row with CI** for CSF-mu-hat vs CSF-1 (and onset-only vs CSF-1), labelled secondary, and restate the contribution around 'probe + simple force rule + CRC'. Make clear in the abstract and contributions that the learner is optional.

[paper-level] Improve readability. Replace internal document codes (07, 08a, 08c, 08e, 08f-08h) with descriptive names (pre-registration, pilot amendment, primary CRC grid, post hoc grid). Add a compact hypothesis glossary table. Trim repeated caveats in the abstract, introduction and discussion so that each caveat is stated once in full and referenced elsewhere.
[paper-level] Resolve the apparent H2b inconsistency in Table 2 by renaming the label-route decision (e.g. 'within +/-0.10, secondary, not decision-bearing') to match the text.

[paper-level] Expand related work to cover classic incipient-slip friction estimation and human grip-force regulation literature. State precisely what is new relative to 'lower force until slip' friction reading.
[paper-level] Render Figure 1 from the actual data, including panel (b) from the real per-stratum monotonised risk curves rather than a schematic.

[paper-level] Use the existing rows to probe the untested explanations. Stratify the H2-R loss by detector error and family, relate the D3 cell margins to the hidden-amplitude variance, and report these analyses as exploratory.

[evidence-level] Add stronger non-tactile and tactile baselines: a non-tactile conformal baseline with a noisy friction proxy (or a pool in which friction correlates with observable attributes), a 'probe plus hand-set margin' rule, and a reactive slip-tightening controller, each evaluated at the same alpha.

[evidence-level] Run the online study with the CRC lambda-hat warm start and physical direct-replay feedback on more than one ordering. If feasible, increase power or equalise oracle/tracker slip so that H3 can be decided.

[evidence-level] Ground sigma with at least a small physical measurement of onset-detection noise on a real gripper/tactile sensor, or a higher-fidelity soft-contact simulation, so that the operating point is not purely assumed.
